DONT BUY THIS GAME. PATCH 11.0 KILL THE GAME.
Writing this right after my first Prismatic run (no Countdown) — in CO-OP. Everything here is about the CO-OP experience on Prismatic difficulty.
I’ve been playing since 2023, always coming back for updates. There’s been good and bad, but this… this is by far the worst experience I’ve ever had with the game.

1) The hub area
They changed the hub location. It used to be a beautiful, small island — nothing unnecessary, everything within reach. At night or during sunset, it had stunning ocean views. Sometimes I’d log in just to run around it (there was a little parkour section). It felt meditative.
Now it’s a huge, ugly, empty space. The foliage looks terrible, and those massive pillars don’t fit the old aesthetic at all. Instead of extending the map lengthwise to fit new weapons and items, the dev just made it wider — and worse.

2) The new “large” maps
At first, I was happy — I thought these would be in addition to the classic maps, since we used to get cool new maps for different biomes.
But NO. Now we’re forced to always play on these “large” maps that are completely empty and soulless. They’re just open fields with a few random pillars.
My favorite automatic shotgun doesn’t even work properly on them anymore. It used to have unlimited range, now it only hits nearby enemies. On these new maps, I literally couldn’t hit 95% of enemies because they were too far away.

3) The map boundaries
You could maybe tolerate the new maps, but the dev removed the location boundaries that used to work perfectly and kept you inside the intended area.
You still want to back up while shooting enemies ahead — but now you’ll step outside the map without realizing it, because you can’t see where the border is.
Then you try to run back into the arena… only to find the same horde of enemies waiting for you. So now you’re fighting both the enemies and the map itself.

4) Weapon build philosophy
The weapon build system used to be really unique. You could make almost any weapon work, even with minimum accuracy. For example, a rocket launcher with full pattern-modifying bullets — it was awesome.
Now the game feels like Risk of Rain 2, and that’s a huge downgrade. To be effective, you need to stack 10 identical perks, ideally ones that give you plain damage with no downsides.
As a result, the first 20–30 islands are pure misery — you deal no damage, enemies have massive HP, and there’s nothing you can do. The enemy scaling outpaces yours. It’s not “hard”; it’s frustrating.
Our only winning run came from an AirStrike + turret build, purely because we got lucky with a legendary laser turret perk and managed to stack 10 “enchant turret” perks plus a turret HP ring.
By the end, I was spamming AirStrike every second — that’s literally the only reason we won. Every attempt at building around normal weapons failed miserably.

5) Elite enemies
Now elites can spawn on any map, not just boss arenas.
Welcome to claustrophobic hell — no room to dodge, enemies in front, a wall behind, and a million explosive barrels rolling toward you. Time to start a new run.

6) The immortal snail
Continuing from the previous issue — there’s now an immortal snail that always chases you. Touch it once and you die instantly.
Good luck surviving in a narrow corridor when you’ve got elites in front and the snail blocking your escape. You’re forced to run toward the enemies, which you should never have to do.

7) One of the most brilliant ideas that actually used to work — but doesn’t anymore.
When your friend dies, you have to stand in their death zone to revive them.
Now there’s an immortal snail chasing you, killing you with one touch.
Need I even say the dev probably doesn’t have any friends?

8) The Prismatic difficulty emblem
The new Prismatic difficulty icon is just awful. It’s a plain gray diamond. JUST GRAY! It looks terrible — I honestly hope they just forgot to color it.

9) The new textures for chests and rocks look awful — like some AI model from Unreal Engine 5.
Why do I need these over-detailed Clash of Clans–style chests when we used to have cool, minimalist, and stylish ones — same with the totems.

I just hate the new "out of bounds" message.
I hate the immortal snail.
I hate the new empty fields.
I hate the new balance.
And you’ll hate them too in your prismatic run.
Keep the money. Bring back the previous patch.

Crab Champions Review: A Shell of a Good Time
Crab Champions is a fast-paced roguelike shooter that proves crabs aren’t just for the beach—they’re for bullet-dodging, loot-collecting mayhem too. Developed by Noisestorm, the game takes the simple premise of crustacean combat and transforms it into an addictive, high-energy experience that keeps players coming back for more.

Gameplay: Every Run Feels Fresh
At its core, Crab Champions is a roguelike, meaning no two runs are ever the same. Whether you're diving into solo play or teaming up with friends in co-op, every session brings a different combination of weapons, abilities, and challenges. The game throws waves of enemies at you, from aggressive sea creatures to mechanical threats, all while rewarding you with power-ups that stack in ridiculous and creative ways.

The movement is fluid and surprisingly deep—dashing, sliding, and double-jumping as a crab feels incredibly satisfying. Mastering movement and aiming is key, as every fight turns into a high-speed dance of dodging enemy fire while unloading your own.

Combat and Upgrades: The Right Kind of Chaotic
Weapons range from basic pistols to shotguns and explosive launchers, each feeling unique and responsive. The true fun comes from the perks you collect along the way—modifiers that can turn your crab into an unstoppable force. One run, you might have a rapid-fire sniper build that melts enemies from a distance; the next, you could be a melee juggernaut dealing electrified ground slams.

Synergy between upgrades is where Crab Champions really shines. The game rewards experimentation, and you’ll constantly discover absurdly overpowered combinations that make you feel unstoppable—until you hit the next difficulty spike and get humbled in an instant.

Replayability: Endless Fun in Bite-Sized Runs
Each run is relatively short, making Crab Champions the perfect game for quick sessions or long playthroughs. Even when you lose, it's hard to be frustrated because every run feels like an opportunity to try new builds. The different biomes, enemy types, and randomly generated upgrades ensure you’ll never get bored.

The difficulty ramps up in a way that keeps things engaging, and with leaderboards and challenges, there’s always a reason to jump back in. The game’s soundtrack—composed by Noisestorm himself—is a high-energy mix that keeps the adrenaline pumping as you blast through hordes of enemies.

Final Verdict: A Hidden Gem Worth Playing
Crab Champions is one of those games that’s easy to pick up but hard to put down. Whether you’re looking for a solo challenge or a fun game to play with friends, it delivers an exciting and unpredictable experience every time.

Pros:
✔️ Fast, smooth, and addictive gameplay
✔️ Highly replayable with endless build variety
✔️ Fun solo or in co-op with friends
✔️ Satisfying movement and combat mechanics
✔️ Great music that keeps the energy high

Cons:
❌ Visuals can get chaotic, making it hard to track enemies
❌ Some upgrades feel stronger than others, leading to imbalance

Score: 9/10
If you love roguelikes, bullet-hell action, and absurdly fun combat, Crab Champions is a must-play. It’s a game where every session is different, and no matter how many times you get knocked down, you’ll want to jump right back in for another round. 🦀💥
